title: status-light settings
description: Settings for the router's LCD and the USB status boards, stored on the router as /etc/status-light.json. Every key is optional; a missing key uses the built-in default.

brightness.description: Backlight while the flame shows, in percent. GL's screen UI uses its own brightness when awake.

boards.description: Per-board settings, keyed by the board's USB serial number as shown in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/serial (e.g. "A0:F2:62:E1:35:58"). netled sends them to the board when it connects and whenever this file changes.

name.description: A label for people; the board ignores it.

brightness.description: Brightness in percent. The T-Display applies it to its backlight, the ESP32-S3-Zero to its LED and strip.

strip.description: An addressable LED strip on the board (the ESP32-S3-Zero drives one on GPIO2). Online, a soft glow sweeps along it from end to end and back.

leds.description: Number of LEDs on the strip, 0 to turn it off. A strip cannot report its length: set identify to count them.

speed.description: How fast the glow sweeps, 1 (one round trip in about 20 s) to 100 (about 2 s).

width.description: How far the glow spreads either side of its centre, in LEDs.

identify.description: Show a counting pattern instead of the status: the first LED green, every 10th red, the rest dim blue. Count them, set leds, then turn this off.

wisps.description: The flame the LCDs show: glowing ribbons (WispParams in firmware/flame). Omitted keys keep the defaults.

strands.description: Number of ribbons. More is denser but slower to draw; the T-Display holds about 25 fps at the default 48.

height.description: Height of the tallest ribbons, in percent of the screen height.

sway.description: How far the ribbons swing sideways, 0 (straight) to 100.

speed.description: Animation speed; 50 is normal, 100 twice as fast.

glow.description: Brightness of the glow; 50 is normal, 100 twice as bright.

width.description: Ribbon width; 50 is normal, 0 draws single lines.
